purpose: Teach: 悗/薀/ワット/塁/モル/代打/士官/コミンテルン

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、漢字の悗、つまり「悗悗」、つまり「悗」の古典用法の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper on classical kanji usage — on the etymology of 悗 and its historical applications — that was a fascinating topic.
lines.style: Warm, genuinely interested. Slight uptick in tone as she acknowledges his work. Measured pace. Leaning forward slightly, giving him full attention.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、薀蓄、つまり薀の語源研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I focused on the etymological roots of 薀 and how the concept evolved over time.
lines.style: Steady, careful response. Slight hesitation at the start, gathering his thoughts. Earnest but not defensive. Speaking precisely because precision matters to him.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、電力単位のワットの歴史研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And if I remember correctly, you explored the history of the watt in electrical engineering — quite a specialized angle.
lines.style: Gently probing, testing her memory. Warm but observant. A pause before the question, as if she's already sensing a mismatch coming.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、野球の塁、つまり塁間の戦術研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Actually, no — I researched base-running tactics in baseball, the strategic spacing between bases and how teams approach that.
lines.style: Quietly correcting, not apologetic. Matter-of-fact but not cold. A small exhale before starting, settling into what he actually studied.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、化学のモル、つまりモル数の概念研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Right, of course. And your chemistry research — the molar concept, mole theory — I thought that's what you were working on.
lines.style: Pausing mid-thought, slightly embarrassed. Warm but clearly confused now. Slower pace, more hesitant. She's realizing the pattern.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、野球の代打、つまり代打起用の統計研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: No, it was baseball again — specifically the statistics around pinch-hitting and how managers deploy substitute batters.
lines.style: Calm, patient. Speaking as if explaining gently to someone who's genuinely trying. No frustration, just clarity. A small note of acceptance in his tone.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、明治期の士官、つまり将校制度の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: I apologize, Ren — I seem to have gotten your papers mixed up. Tell me again: was it Meiji military officers and the officers' corps system you researched?
lines.style: Slow, measured admission. Slightly sheepish but not defensive. She's laughing at herself a little internally. Genuine curiosity now, wanting to actually listen.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、戦間期のコミンテルン、つまり共産主義インターの研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: No, that was during the interwar period — I researched the Comintern, the international communist movement and its organizational structure.
lines.style: Final correction, delivered with steady kindness. Not triumphant, just clear. Speaking as if he understands she was trying all along. Soft close, almost gentle.
